sections.html:
American Fork sits in north-central Utah County at the foot of Mount Timpanogos, just north of Utah Lake and about 32 miles southeast of Salt Lake City. The ZIP code is 84003. Population climbed from 33,337 in 2020 to an estimated 41,020 in mid-2025, nearly a quarter in five years.

The typical household has 3.19 people, and the median home value is $496,700. About 65.8% of homes are owner-occupied. Buyers in a family-heavy market often shop for bedrooms, a yard and parking, so lead with those when you describe the house.

FrontRunner commuter rail has stopped in American Fork since 2012, and Interstate 15 runs alongside town. A house near the station or the freeway has a commute advantage worth mentioning.

American Fork's public schools belong to the Alpine School District today, and that district dissolves on July 1, 2027. A June 2026 news report places American Fork in a new district called Aspen Peaks, together with Lehi, Highland, Alpine and Cedar Hills. The other two new districts are Lake Mountain and Timpanogos.

Utah County approved the new boundaries in March 2025, and they largely follow city lines. Buyers with children will ask where the house lands, so check the county's boundary maps if your lot sits near an edge.

Two utility details come up with American Fork buyers.

  • The city runs a pressurized irrigation system that delivers untreated water to lawns and gardens. It was built from 2007 to 2010, and about 95% of residents are connected. Meters are installed on connections, and billing by usage was planned to start with the 2025 irrigation season.
  • Sewer treatment comes from the Timpanogos Special Service District, which also serves neighboring towns. Its rates rose 40% on January 1, 2024, 15% in 2025 and another 15% on January 1, 2026. The city's own sewer charges did not change.
  • The city's water plan sets a single-family base rate of $16.17 a month for a three-quarter-inch meter, with no volume charge for the first 3,000 gallons.

City Hall is at 51 East Main Street, phone 801-763-3000. The city's online Report a Concern form takes code enforcement, road, sidewalk and sewer complaints. For a final bill, call before closing.

sections.h2: How property tax works in American Fork
sections.html:
Three Utah County offices shape your bill. The Assessor decides market value, the Auditor mails a Notice of Property Valuation and Tax Changes every July, and the Treasurer follows with the tax notice in mid to late October.

Homes lived in by owners, and long-term rentals, can qualify for the primary residential exemption, which leaves 55% of market value taxable. Qualifying means 183 consecutive days of occupancy or more in a year. After a purchase or ownership change, the county mails a Residential Property Declaration. Tell your buyer to watch for that letter and send it back on time.

Utah County offices at 100 East Center St, Provo

The Treasurer's email is treasurer@utahcounty.gov. To contest the value, file with the Utah County Board of Equalization online, by email, by mail or in person. Your valuation notice shows the deadline.

sections.h2: Earthquake risk and recording a deed
sections.html:
American Fork lies on the Wasatch Front, where the Provo segment of the Wasatch Fault produced a major earthquake about 200 to 700 years ago. The whole fault runs about 240 miles, and about 80% of Utah's people live along it. Buyers may ask about chimneys, foundations and past retrofit work.

Older homes in the older core of town are the ones most likely to prompt these questions. If yours has had work done, a one-page list of what was fixed, when, and by whom gives a buyer more comfort than a verbal promise.

The Utah County Recorder files the deed at the Provo address above. Recorder staff do not prepare or notarize documents, give legal advice or search title, so the title company or an attorney handles that step.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in American Fork?
sections.html:
Since nobody is waiting on loan approval, the timeline depends on title work and on how fast any lien payoffs arrive. Sellers with a clear title often close within a short stretch, while an inherited house with several heirs takes longer because every signature has to be gathered first.

Take a standard closing and remove the lender: that is a cash sale. The sequence runs like this.

  1. Both sides sign the purchase agreement.
  2. Escrow opens at a title company, which searches title.
  3. Any mortgage or lien gets a payoff demand.
  4. You sign the deed and a closing statement listing what each side pays, payoffs included.
  5. The deed is filed in Provo and funds reach you.

Pull your latest tax notice, loan payoff details and roof age together first. A tenant means lease dates should be ready too, so move-out terms can go into the contract.

sections.h2: Paperwork to gather before you talk to a buyer
sections.html:
Most of what you need comes from the offices already named above, and having it ready saves days.

  • The newest Utah County tax notice, so the title company can see what is paid and what is open.
  • Any Residential Property Declaration letter you received after buying, and proof you returned it.
  • Mortgage or lien payoff details, since escrow requests payoff demands from each lender.
  • Lease dates and rent amounts, if a tenant lives there.
  • Records of foundation, chimney or roof work, because earthquake and roof questions are common along the Wasatch Front.
  • A recent city sewer or irrigation statement, so the buyer sees what the utilities cost.

Once these are in your folder, escrow opens fast and a closing date can be chosen to suit you. No lender has to sign off on anything, so the pace is yours.

Tax is billed once a year. At closing the title company divides the current bill between you and the buyer by closing date and covers any unpaid balance out of your proceeds. See that split spelled out on the closing statement.

Utilities are handled apart from escrow. Phone the city at 801-763-3000 to stop water and irrigation on the closing date and say where the last bill should be mailed. Because irrigation is metered, request a final reading when you schedule the stop.

Common reasons to call a cash buyer here: an inherited house, a tenant who must leave, repairs that cost more than you have, or a move that cannot wait. What they share is wanting a fixed closing date without haggling over a lender appraiser's repair list.

Selling as-is puts the condition on the buyer, as you describe it. A retail buyer's price moves with repairs, so compare each repair's cost with what it adds before spending.

faqs.q: Which county is American Fork in?
faqs.a: Utah County. Its Assessor sets value, its Auditor mails the notice, and its Treasurer in Provo collects the tax.

faqs.q: Which school district will American Fork be in after 2027?
faqs.a: The new Aspen Peaks district, based on a June 2026 news report. The Alpine School District dissolves into three districts on July 1, 2027.

faqs.q: Does the residential exemption apply to American Fork homes?
faqs.a: Yes, for primary residences and long-term rentals, which are taxed on 55% of market value. Occupancy must reach 183 consecutive days in a year, and a buyer may need to file a declaration.

faqs.q: Who treats American Fork's sewage, and did rates change?
faqs.a: The Timpanogos Special Service District. Its charges rose 40% in January 2024, 15% in 2025 and 15% in January 2026, while the city's own sewer charges stayed the same.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for an American Fork house?
faqs.a: Take it to the Utah County Recorder in Suite 1300 at 100 East Center Street, Provo, or call 801-851-8179. Staff will not prepare the document.
